page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Schizocarpic — definition
lines: Dry fruits that split at maturity into
one-seeded pieces called mericarps are known
steps.why: Schizo = to split: the ripe fruit breaks into one-seeded units (mericarps) - splitting into mericarps is the whole definition.
common_mistakes: Confusing schizocarpic with dehiscent fruits. Dehiscent fruits open and release SEEDS; schizocarpic fruits break into one-seeded PIECES.
steps.memory_tip: Schizo - splits; each split piece keeps one seed.
steps.margin_note: Definition must contain the word mericarp.

steps.label: Example
steps.why: The book's examples are Acacia and castor; the bracketed type names (lomentum, regma) identify which schizocarpic fruit each one is.
common_mistakes: Giving pea as the example. The pea pod is a dehiscent legume, not schizocarpic.
steps.memory_tip: Acacia pod breaks bead by bead; castor splits into three.
steps.margin_note: One example is asked; the type names in brackets are a bonus.
